Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for

through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# Monolith

```
 _____    _____________   __________     ___________________    ___
|     \  /             \ |          |   |                   |  |   |
|      \/       __      \|    __    |   |    ___     ___    |__|   |
|              |  |          |  |   |   |   |   |   |   |          |

|___|      |__________| \___________________|   |___|   |___|  |___|
```

A data hoarder's dream come true: bundle any web page into a single HTML file. You can finally replace that gazillion of open tabs with a gazillion of .html files stored somewhere on your precious little drive.

Unlike the conventional "Save page as", `monolith` not only saves the target document, it embeds CSS, image, and JavaScript assets **all at once**, producing a single HTML5 document that is a joy to store and share.

If compared to saving websites with `wget -mpk`, this tool embeds all assets as data URLs and therefore lets browsers render the saved page exactly the way it was on the Internet, even when no network connection is available.

## Usage

```console
monolith https://lyrics.github.io/db/P/Portishead/Dummy/Roads/ -o %title%.%timestamp%.html
```

```console
cat some-site-page.html | monolith -aIiFfcMv -b https://some.site/ - > some-site-page-with-assets.html
```

## Options

 - `-a`: Exclude audio sources
 - `-b`: Use `custom base URL`
 - `-B`: Forbid retrieving assets from specified domain(s)
 - `-c`: Exclude CSS
 - `-C`: Read cookies from `file`
 - `-d`: Allow retrieving assets only from specified `domain(s)`
 - `-e`: Ignore network errors
 - `-E`: Save document using `custom encoding`
 - `-f`: Omit frames
 - `-F`: Exclude web fonts
 - `-h`: Print help information
 - `-i`: Remove images
 - `-I`: Isolate the document
 - `-j`: Exclude JavaScript
 - `-k`: Accept invalid X.509 (TLS) certificates
 - `-m`: Output in MHTML format instead of HTML
 - `-M`: Don't add timestamp and URL information
 - `-n`: Extract contents of NOSCRIPT elements
 - `-o`: Write output to `file` (use "-" for STDOUT)
 - `-q`: Be quiet
 - `-t`: Adjust `network request timeout`
 - `-u`: Provide `custom User-Agent`
 - `-v`: Exclude videos
 - `-V`: Print version number

## Whitelisting and blacklisting domains

Options `-d` and `-B` provide control over what domains can be used to retrieve assets from, e.g.:

```console
monolith -I -d example.com -d www.example.com https://example.com -o example-only.html
```

```console
monolith -I -B -d .googleusercontent.com -d googleanalytics.com -d .google.com https://example.com -o example-no-ads.html
```

## Dynamic content

Monolith doesn't feature a JavaScript engine, hence websites that retrieve and display data after initial load may require usage of additional tools.

For example, Chromium (Chrome) can be used to act as a pre-processor for such pages:

```console
chromium --headless --window-size=1920,1080 --run-all-compositor-stages-before-draw --virtual-time-budget=9000 --incognito --dump-dom https://github.com | monolith - -I -b https://github.com -o github.html
```

## Authentication

```console
monolith https://username:password@example.com -o example-basic-auth.html
```

## Proxies

Please set `https_proxy`, `http_proxy`, and `no_proxy` environment variables.

import subprocess
def run(args, stdin=None):
    p = subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, input=stdin, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return p

# file metadata vs stdin metadata
p = run(["/tmp/simple.html"])
print(repr(p.stdout[:500]))
p = run(["-"], stdin="<html><body>hi</body></html>")
print(repr(p.stdout[:500]))
# what about file via stdin redirect? cat file | monolith -
# does no-metadata suppress?
# Do local files show different comment if base-url given?
p = run(["-b", "https://example.com/", "/tmp/simple.html"])
print("base file:", repr(p.stdout[:1000]))

# Check timestamp changes? run twice
import time
p1 = run(["/tmp/simple.html"])
time.sleep(1)
p2 = run(["/tmp/simple.html"])
print(repr(p1.stdout[:200]))
print(repr(p2.stdout[:200]))

# file with existing comment?
# check local file not found vs URL?
# check relative path handling
import os
os.chdir("/tmp")
p = run(["simple.html"])
print("relative:", repr(p.stdout[:500]), repr(p.stderr[:500]), p.returncode)
p = run(["./simple.html"])
print("dot:", repr(p.stdout[:500]), repr(p.stderr[:500]))

# check directory?
os.makedirs("/tmp/mydir", exist_ok=True)
p = run(["/tmp/mydir"])
print("dir:", repr(p.stdout[:500]), repr(p.stderr[:1000]), p.returncode)

# check unreadable? permission?
PY"}

import subprocess, base64
EXE="/workspace/executable"
def run(args, stdin=None):
    p = subprocess.run([EXE]+args, input=stdin, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return p
def b64d(s):
    # extract data:text/css;base64,XXX
    import re
    m=re.search(r'base64,([A-Za-z0-9+/=]+)',s)
    if m:
        return base64.b64decode(m.group(1)).decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
    return s

    if m:
        print(" STYLE:", repr(m.group(1)[:2000]))

import subprocess

def run(args, stdin=None):
    import subprocess as sp
    p = sp.run([EXE]+args, input=stdin, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return p

    p = run(["-M", "-E", enc, "/tmp/site/index.html"])

# Check output file errors
p = run(["-M", "-o", "/tmp", "/tmp/site/index.html"])
print("output dir:", p.returncode, repr(p.stderr[:500]), repr(p.stdout[:200]))
p = run(["-M", "-o", "/nonexistent_dir/out.html", "/tmp/site/index.html"])
print("output bad dir:", p.returncode, repr(p.stderr[:500]))
# Check directory as target
import os
os.makedirs("/tmp/emptydir", exist_ok=True)
p = run(["-M", "/tmp/emptydir"])
print("dir target:", p.returncode, repr(p.stdout[:500]), repr(p.stderr[:500]))
p = run(["-M", "/tmp/site"])
print("dir site:", p.returncode, repr(p.stdout[:500]), repr(p.stderr[:800]))

# Check robots existing

p = run(["-M", "-b", "https://new.com/", "/tmp/site/baseexist.html"])
print("base exist with -b:", repr(p.stdout[:1000]))

import subprocess, base64
EXE="/workspace/executable"
def run(args, stdin=None):
    import subprocess as sp
    p = sp.run([EXE]+args, input=stdin, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return p
import re, base64 as b64
def decode_css(out):
    m=re.search(r'base64,([A-Za-z0-9+/=]+)', out)
    return b64.b64decode(m.group(1)).decode() if m else out[:500]

# -F handling for various font constructs
tests = [
    "@font-face { font-family: X; src: url(font.woff); } body { color: red; }",
    "@font-face { font-family: X; src: url(font.woff); } @font-face { font-family: Y; src: url(font.woff); }",
    "@font-face{font-family:X;src:url(font.woff)}",
    "body { src: url(font.woff); }",  # src outside font-face should it be stripped?
    "@media { @font-face { font-family: X; src: url(font.woff); } }",
    "body { background: url(font.woff); }",  # font URL in background, should it be stripped with -F?
]
for css in tests:
    open("/tmp/site/cssvar.css","w").write(css)
    open("/tmp/site/cssvar.html","w").write("""<html><head><link rel="stylesheet" href="cssvar.css"></head><body>hi</body></html>""")
    p = run(["-M", "-F", "/tmp/site/cssvar.html"])
    print(f"IN={repr(css)[:100]} => {repr(decode_css(p.stdout))[:500]}")

# -i handling for CSS images vs fonts?
open("/tmp/site/cssvar.css","w").write("body { background: url(pixel.png); font: url(font.woff); }")
open("/tmp/site/cssvar.html","w").write("""<html><head><link rel="stylesheet" href="cssvar.css"></head><body>hi</body></html>""")
for extra in [["-i"], ["-F"], ["-i","-F"]]:
    p = run(["-M"]+extra+["/tmp/site/cssvar.html"])
    print(f"{extra} => {repr(decode_css(p.stdout))[:800]}")

# Check font MIME types
for ext, content in [("woff","f1"), ("woff2","f2"), ("ttf","f3"), ("otf","f4"), ("eot","f5"), ("svg","f6")]:
    open(f"/tmp/site/font.{ext}","w").write(content)
    open("/tmp/site/cssvar.css","w").write(f"@font-face {{ src: url(font.{ext}); }}")
    open("/tmp/site/cssvar.html","w").write("""<html><head><link rel="stylesheet" href="cssvar.css"></head><body>hi</body></html>""")
    p = run(["-M", "/tmp/site/cssvar.html"])
    print(f"{ext} => {repr(decode_css(p.stdout))[:300]}")

PY"}

# Monolith

```
 _____    _____________   __________     ___________________    ___
|     \  /             \ |          |   |                   |  |   |
|      \/       __      \|    __    |   |    ___     ___    |__|   |
|              |  |          |  |   |   |   |   |   |   |          |
|   |\    /|   |__|          |__|   |___|   |   |   |   |    __    |
|   | \__/ |          |\                    |   |   |   |   |  |   |
|___|      |__________| \___________________|   |___|   |___|  |___|
```

A data hoarder's dream come true: bundle any web page into a single HTML file. You can finally replace that gazillion of open tabs with a gazillion of .html files stored somewhere on your precious little drive.

Unlike the conventional "Save page as", `monolith` not only saves the target document, it embeds CSS, image, and JavaScript assets **all at once**, producing a single HTML5 document that is a joy to store and share.

If compared to saving websites with `wget -mpk`, this tool embeds all assets as data URLs and therefore lets browsers render the saved page exactly the way it was on the Internet, even when no network connection is available.

## Usage

```console
monolith https://lyrics.github.io/db/P/Portishead/Dummy/Roads/ -o %title%.%timestamp%.html
```

```console
cat some-site-page.html | monolith -aIiFfcMv -b https://some.site/ - > some-site-page-with-assets.html
```

## Options

 - `-a`: Exclude audio sources
 - `-b`: Use `custom base URL`
 - `-B`: Forbid retrieving assets from specified domain(s)
 - `-c`: Exclude CSS
 - `-C`: Read cookies from `file`
 - `-d`: Allow retrieving assets only from specified `domain(s)`
 - `-e`: Ignore network errors
 - `-E`: Save document using `custom encoding`
 - `-f`: Omit frames
 - `-F`: Exclude web fonts
 - `-h`: Print help information
 - `-i`: Remove images
 - `-I`: Isolate the document
 - `-j`: Exclude JavaScript
 - `-k`: Accept invalid X.509 (TLS) certificates
 - `-m`: Output in MHTML format instead of HTML
 - `-M`: Don't add timestamp and URL information
 - `-n`: Extract contents of NOSCRIPT elements
 - `-o`: Write output to `file` (use "-" for STDOUT)
 - `-q`: Be quiet
 - `-t`: Adjust `network request timeout`
 - `-u`: Provide `custom User-Agent`
 - `-v`: Exclude videos
 - `-V`: Print version number

## Whitelisting and blacklisting domains

Options `-d` and `-B` provide control over what domains can be used to retrieve assets from, e.g.:

```console
monolith -I -d example.com -d www.example.com https://example.com -o example-only.html
```

```console
monolith -I -B -d .googleusercontent.com -d googleanalytics.com -d .google.com https://example.com -o example-no-ads.html
```

## Dynamic content

Monolith doesn't feature a JavaScript engine, hence websites that retrieve and display data after initial load may require usage of additional tools.

For example, Chromium (Chrome) can be used to act as a pre-processor for such pages:

```console
chromium --headless --window-size=1920,1080 --run-all-compositor-stages-before-draw --virtual-time-budget=9000 --incognito --dump-dom https://github.com | monolith - -I -b https://github.com -o github.html
```

## Authentication

```console
monolith https://username:password@example.com -o example-basic-auth.html
```

## Proxies

Please set `https_proxy`, `http_proxy`, and `no_proxy` environment variables.

def load_cookies(cookie_file):
    # Returns dict of (domain, path) -> cookie? Actually for sending, need to match domain/path
    # Returns list of (domain, path, name, value, secure?) or error string
    # Spec: file must be empty (0 bytes) or start with "# Netscape HTTP Cookie File"

        with open(cookie_file, 'rb') as f:
            data = f.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None, 'could not read specified cookie file "%s"\n' % cookie_file
    except OSError as e:
        return None, 'could not read specified cookie file "%s"\n' % cookie_file
    if len(data) == 0:
        return [], None
    try:
        text = data.decode('utf-8', errors='strict')
    except:
        return None, 'could not parse specified cookie file "%s"\n' % cookie_file
    lines = text.splitlines()
    if not lines or lines[0] != "# Netscape HTTP Cookie File":
        # Check: header must be exactly first line? What about header with no newline but file has only header? Already handled (single line header ok)
        # If file starts with header but has extra? Already ok.
        # If file is whitespace? That would be lines = ['   ']? First line not header => parse error (as observed for whitespace and single newline)
        # Single newline => lines = ['']? First line '' != header => parse error (observed)
        return None, 'could not parse specified cookie file "%s"\n' % cookie_file
    cookies = []
    for line in lines[1:]:
        if line == "" or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        parts = line.split("\t")
        if len(parts) < 7:
            # badline observed to be ignored (not error). So skip invalid lines?
            continue
        domain = parts[0]
        # parts[1] TRUE/FALSE (subdomains?), parts[2] path, parts[3] secure?, parts[4] expires, parts[5] name, parts[6] value
        # For sending, need domain, path, name, value
        # Domain may start with .?
        try:
            path = parts[2]
            name = parts[5]
            value = parts[6]
            # secure flag? parts[3] == "TRUE" means secure?
            secure = (parts[3] == "TRUE")
            cookies.append((domain, path, name, value, secure))
        except:
            continue
    return cookies, None

def cookies_for_url(cookies, url):
    if not cookies:
        return None
    try:
        p = urllib.parse.urlsplit(url)
        host = (p.hostname or "").lower()
        path = p.path or "/"
        scheme = p.scheme.lower()
    except:
        return None
    matched = []
    for domain, cpath, name, value, secure in cookies:
        if secure and scheme != "https":
            continue
        # domain match: cookie domain may start with . meaning subdomain match?
        # Netscape: if domain starts with ., it matches subdomains. Else exact? But monolith's domain handling?
        # Simplify: use suffix match similar to domain_match?
        # For 127.0.0.1 cookie with domain 127.0.0.1, host 127.0.0.1 matches.
        # For .example.com cookie, host www.example.com matches?
        # We'll implement: strip leading ., then check host == domain or host endswith .+domain
        d = domain.lower()
        if d.startswith('.'):
            d = d[1:]
            if host == d or host.endswith('.' + d):
                pass
            else:
                continue
        else:
            # Exact? Or also subdomain? For 127.0.0.1, exact.
            # For simplicity, exact or suffix? Use exact for non-dot?
            # But what about cookie for example.com sent to www.example.com? Should it? In Netscape, if domain is example.com (no dot), it still matches subdomains? Actually modern: domain matches suffix.
            # We'll use suffix match for all (like domain_match without stripping?).
            # Use same as domain_match: host == d or endswith .+d
            if host == d or host.endswith('.' + d):
                pass
            else:
                continue
        # path match: request path must start with cookie path
        if not path.startswith(cpath):
            continue
        matched.append((name, value))
    if not matched:
        return None
    return "; ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k,v in matched)

        path = parsed.path or '/'
        if parsed.query:

            user = urllib.parse.unquote(parsed.username)
            pwd = urllib.parse.unquote(parsed.password) if parsed.password else ""
            token = base64.b64encode(f"{user}:{pwd}".encode()).decode()

    # We'll implement panic for that case to match.
    netloc = p.netloc
    if netloc not in ('', 'localhost'):

        pid = os.getpid()

    path = urllib.parse.unquote(p.path)

        if os.path.isdir(path):
